explanation: The December 2016 document explicitly attributes the post-November-election market break to 'revised expectations for government spending and tax policy following the U.S. elections in early November,' identifying this as the primary driver of substantially higher Treasury yields, rising equity indexes, a stronger dollar, and narrower credit spreads — all consistent with a structural break on 2016-11-07 (the day after the U.S. presidential election). The document also records a 25bp rate hike (target range raised to 1/2–3/4 percent) and a steepening of the anticipated federal funds rate path, confirming a material shift in the monetary policy outlook directly linked to the flagged date.
